name: Mobile Application Security (Android & iOS)
tagline: Testing your own or authorized Android & iOS apps: static analysis, decompilation, runtime instrumentation, traffic interception, and attack-surface automation.

tools.name: MobSF (Mobile Security Framework)
tools.desc: Automated all-in-one analyzer for APK, IPA, and Windows mobile binaries: permissions, exported components, insecure manifest/crypto config, hardcoded secrets, and OWASP MASTG-style checks surfaced in a clean web UI plus REST API for CI.
tools.when: Always the first pass on an app binary you are authorized to test — upload the APK or IPA, read the findings report, then drill into specific hits for manual follow-up.

tools.name: Quark-Engine
tools.desc: Obfuscation-neglect APK scoring engine (distinct from the old LinkedIn 'qark'): matches the app's call graph against a rule set of suspicious behaviors — crypto misuse, dynamic dex loading, accessibility/SMS abuse, C2 calls — and emits confidence-scored reports.
tools.when: Quick second opinion on an APK for risky behavior patterns after MobSF, or to generate new detection rules from code you reverse yourself.

tools.name: APKiD
tools.desc: YARA-based detector for packers, protectors, and obfuscators (DexProtector, Bangcle, qihoo, etc.) inside an APK/DEX before any reversing effort begins.
tools.when: Scope a hardened app early: knowing it is packed tells you static-only analysis is not enough and you will need runtime dexdump (frida-dexdump).

tools.name: jadx
tools.desc: One-step DEX-to-Java decompiler with GUI and CLI that rebuilds readable Java source, resources, and AndroidManifest.xml into a searchable whole-project view.
tools.when: Default decompilation of a fresh APK: navigate the reconstructed project, follow flows across classes, and copy logic into notes.
tools.install: Download the latest zip from GitHub releases (or 'brew install jadx')

tools.name: apktool
tools.desc: Decodes Android resources and AndroidManifest.xml into editable form and rebuilds the APK; exposes smali/baksmali bytecode for patching when Java source is not needed.
tools.when: Modify res/ or smali and repackage the APK (behavior/repackage tests), or pull the manifest cleanly when jadx output gets mangled.
tools.install: Download the jar wrapper from GitHub releases (or 'sudo apt install apktool')

tools.name: frida-dexdump
tools.desc: Dumps in-memory DEX files from a running app via Frida, defeating packers and protectors that only materialize code at runtime.
tools.when: Analyze a packed/hardened app: launch it on a device, dump the loaded dex at runtime, then feed the recovered classes back into jadx.

tools.name: dex2jar
tools.desc: The classic DEX-to-JAR converter (paired with JD-GUI for a quick Java view); effectively unmaintained but still the format older guides and toolchains expect.
tools.when: Legacy fallback decompile when jadx chokes on an unusual format, or when a downstream tooling chain requires .jar/.class input.

tools.name: Frida
tools.desc: Cross-platform dynamic instrumentation toolkit: inject a frida-server process onto Android/iOS to hook functions, bypass SSL pinning and root detection, trace crypto calls, and invoke internal methods from a Python/JS REPL.
tools.when: The runtime layer of most mobile tests — bypass cert pinning, trace sensitive functions, dump buffers, and poke internals static analysis cannot reach.
tools.install: pip install frida-tools && push a matching-version frida-server to the device

tools.name: objection
tools.desc: Frida-powered runtime exploration toolkit: one-liners to disable SSL pinning and root checks, browse Android/iOS storage (Keychain, SharedPrefs, Bundle), and explore exported classes without writing custom JS.
tools.when: Quick interactive runtime pass on your own app — disable pinning/root detection and inspect stored data — when hand-writing Frida scripts is overkill.

tools.name: Magisk
tools.desc: Systemless rooting framework for physical Android devices and emulators that gives Frida, adb, and your injected agents the root context most dynamic tests need; it is a rooting kit first, not a pentest tool.
tools.when: Prepare a dedicated test device with an unlocked bootloader when an app refuses to run on stock or detects the emulator you were using.
tools.install: Install the Magisk APK or 'fastboot boot magisk_patched-<hash>.img' on an unlocked-bootloader device

tools.name: adb (Android Debug Bridge)
tools.desc: Google's core device bridge from Android platform-tools: install apps, push/pull files, shell in, port-forward, install CA certificates, and capture logcat.
tools.when: Every device setup step — enumerate devices, push frida-server and test certificates, and snapshot app data before and after a test run.

tools.name: mitmproxy
tools.desc: Interactive HTTPS intercepting proxy built for mobile workflows: install its CA on the device, replay or rewrite HTTP/2 and gRPC flows, and script custom handling with Python addons; pair with a Frida/objection pinning bypass to decrypt app TLS.
tools.when: Any network-level test of your own apps — log, tamper, or replay API traffic from a rooted device, emulator, or iOS simulator.

tools.name: Charles Proxy
tools.desc: Commercial GUI HTTPS proxy with click-through SSL proxying, rewrite/breakpoints, and a visual request timeline — the macOS-centric alternative to a terminal proxy.
tools.when: Point-and-click interception and rewriting during manual iOS testing on a workstation when you prefer a GUI over mitmproxy's keyboard-driven flow.
tools.install: Download from charlesproxy.com (trial, then paid license)

tools.name: Drozer
tools.desc: The reference Android attack-surface framework: an on-device agent lets you assume the role of another app and enumerate/exploit exported activities, content providers, services, and broadcast receivers from a console.
tools.when: After static analysis, map the app's IPC/component attack surface and probe each exported component for authorization and data-exposure flaws.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/ReversecLabs/drozer.git && cd drozer && pip install . (plus the drozer agent APK on the device)

tools.name: Android Tamer
tools.desc: Linux distro/VM prebundling dozens of Android-sec tools (jadx, apktool, MobSF, AndroBugs, Frida, radare2). Tamer 4 is end-of-life and Tamer 5 is under construction, so it is a convenience starting point, not a project to build on.
tools.when: Stand up a one-shot preconfigured Android-tools VM for a specific engagement; otherwise skip — each tool here installs more reliably on your own base OS.
tools.install: Download the Tamer 4 VM from TamerPlatform and import into VirtualBox/VMware

tools.name: Frida-iOS
tools.desc: Frida on iOS for hooking, swizzling, and runtime inspection of app classes on jailbroken devices.
tools.when: When you need to trace iOS app runtime behavior on jailbroken devices.

tools.name: Frida-codeshare
tools.desc: Collection of iOS-focused Frida scripts for class dumping and method tracing.
tools.when: Need common iOS hooks without writing your own.
